summary: Take a basis y of L ∩ ker A; with C = (Ax)⁻¹A, the matrix (x | y) has left inverse (C; l − lxC) and spans L.

steps.claim: Let y be a basis matrix of L ∩ ker A with left inverse l (exists_basis_matrix), s its number of columns = dim(L ∩ ker A), and C = (Ax)⁻¹A, so that Cx = 1 and Cy = 0 (Ay = 0 by mul_eq_zero_of_range_le_ker). Then (C; l − lxC) is a left inverse of (x | y); every v ∈ L is x(Cv) + (v − xCv) with v − xCv ∈ L ∩ ker A, so the columns span L; the columns of y lie in L, Ay = 0; and if yt = xu then 0 = Cyt = u, so yt = 0 and t = l(yt) = 0.
steps.lean:
⟨_, (exists_basis_matrix _).imp fun y ⟨⟨l, _⟩, e⟩ ↦ let C := (A * x)⁻¹ * A
  have ⟨p, o⟩ := (le_inf_iff.1 e.le).imp id mul_eq_zero_of_range_le_ker; ⟨rfl, ⟨C.fromRows (l - l *
    x * C), by aesop⟩, le_antisymm (by simp [LE.le, add_mem, hL _, p _]) fun v w ↦ (e.ge ⟨sub_mem w
    (hL ⟨C *ᵥ v, rfl⟩), by simp [C, mulVec_sub, ← A.mul_assoc, h]⟩).imp' (C *ᵥ v ⊕ᵥ ·) (by aesop),
    p, o, fun _ ⟨_, k⟩ ↦ by simpa [C, *, -k] using congr((l - l * x * C) *ᵥ $k).symm⟩⟩
